## What's new

This stable release rolls up dev pre-releases v3.05-dev and v3.06-dev.

**Updating promptly is recommended.**

### Fixed

- **Several gaps have been closed in how the application's own files are owned
  and protected during an update**, and **the update process no longer trusts a
  stored configuration value when deciding where to fetch updates from.** On a
  server running the application, it was possible for the unprivileged account
  the application runs under to obtain more access than it should have. Both
  routes are closed, along with the wider pattern they belonged to — the
  boundary that account is meant to be confined to now holds throughout an
  update, including for the files the updater itself reads and restores from.

- **Account changes now take effect immediately, even under load.** Disabling an
  account, changing a password, resetting one, or deleting a user already ended
  that person's other sessions straight away. Under a narrow combination of
  concurrent traffic, that could be delayed by a few seconds. It no longer can
  be.

### Improved

- **The automated check that guards every API endpoint is more thorough — and
  now checks itself.** Every change to this project runs a check confirming that
  each API endpoint requires a signed-in user. That check could be misled into
  reporting an endpoint as protected when it was not. It now reads the code more
  carefully, and ships with its own test suite so the check's own correctness is
  verified on every run rather than assumed.

### Changed

- **Updates now stop with a clear message instead of continuing** if the
  configured access token is not a well-formed GitHub token, or if the
  repository the installation updates from is not on github.com. Standard
  installations are unaffected — this only surfaces where one of those values
  was already wrong or unusual. Using a self-hosted mirror as the update source
  is no longer supported; such installations could not receive update
  notifications in any case.

- **The "connect a delivery provider" pop-up has been reworked internally** so
  that it will keep working under the stricter browser security policy planned
  for a future release. Its behaviour is unchanged: it still reports success or
  failure, notifies the page that opened it, and closes itself.

Existing installations pick this up automatically on their next scheduled
update. No configuration change is required, and no action is needed beyond
updating.
